INTU.sells: TurboTax for people doing taxes, QuickBooks and Mailchimp for small businesses, and Credit Karma tips.
INTU.moat: Businesses keep years of books and payroll in QuickBooks, and accountants know it, so moving is a hassle.
INTU.grows: More small businesses running payroll, payments and loans through QuickBooks, plus AI helpers.
INTU.risk: Free government tax filing or cheap AI tools that do taxes and bookkeeping could pull customers away.

ADBE.sells: Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator and Acrobat subscriptions paid for by creators, students and companies.
ADBE.moat: Designers learn Photoshop in school and clients expect its files, so teams stick with Adobe tools.
ADBE.grows: Pricier plans with Firefly AI features, plus marketing software sold to big brands.
ADBE.risk: Cheap AI image and video makers and simple apps like Canva could make Adobe's tools feel unneeded.

CRM.sells: Software big companies pay for to track customers and run sales and service teams, plus Slack chat.
CRM.moat: A company's whole customer history and daily work live inside Salesforce, so ripping it out hurts.
CRM.grows: Selling extra tools like Slack, data tools and Agentforce AI agents to companies already using it.
CRM.risk: AI agents from rivals, or ones companies build themselves, could make Salesforce less needed.

PAYX.sells: Payroll, HR, retirement plans and insurance services that small and medium businesses pay for monthly.
PAYX.moat: Getting paychecks and taxes right is scary, so once payroll runs smoothly, owners rarely switch.
PAYX.grows: Clients hiring more workers, plus adding HR, benefits and insurance services to each customer.
PAYX.risk: Cheaper app-based rivals like Gusto, or a slowdown that closes small businesses and cuts jobs.

F.sells: Ford pickups, Bronco and Explorer SUVs, Transit work vans and Lincolns for families and fleets, plus loans.
F.moat: Truck buyers are very loyal to Ford, and businesses rely on its huge dealer and repair network for vans.
F.grows: Ford Pro selling software and service to work fleets, plus hybrid trucks that customers want.
F.risk: Car making is costly and cutthroat; recalls, cheap Chinese EVs and money-losing electric cars hurt it.
